paragraphs.text: Rambam, Laws of Shofar, Sukkah and Lulav 8:15, calls joy in doing a mitzvah and love of the One who commanded it a great form of divine service. He associates that joy with David setting aside his own dignity before God. This illuminates Rav Tzadok’s account of a person who can rejoice in a mitzvah that comes at a personal cost.

paragraphs.text: Gittin 37b: "One who repays a debt to his fellow in the Sabbatical year (Shevi'it) — the lender must say to him: 'I remit it'; and if the borrower said to him, 'Even so,' he may accept it from him, as it is stated: 'And this is the matter [word] of the remission' (Devarim 15:2). Rabbah said: And he may hang him until he says thus. (The lender compels the borrower, and if he has the power to do so, he may even hang him on a tree until the borrower says: 'Even so, I wish to repay the debt to you,' and then the lender may accept his money in accordance with the law.) Abba bar Marta, who is Abba bar Manyumi, owed money to Rabbah (Rabbah had lent him money). He brought it to him in the Sabbatical year (Abba bar Manyumi came to repay it during the Sabbatical year). He (Rabbah) said to him: 'I remit it,' whereupon he took it and left (he took the money back and went away). Abaye came and found him sad (Abaye arrived and found Rabbah sad). He said to him: 'Why is the Master sad?' He said to him: 'Such-and-such happened...'" And in the end, Abaye went and told Abba bar Manyumi to bring the money back and say, "Even so," and he did so, and Rabbah accepted the money.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 61b “The good inclination judges the righteous, as it says, ‘My heart is hollow within me.’ The two inclinations judge the intermediate. Rabbah said, ‘People like us are intermediate.’ Abaye replied, ‘Master, you leave no life for any creature!’” Rav Tzadok quotes Rabbah’s self-description while explaining that Rabbah could still listen to his good inclination and rejoice in a genuine mitzvah. The printed reference here is 60b. The statement occurs at 61b.

paragraphs.text: Divrei Soferim 38:1 “When one merits that Torah becomes a medicine of life, it is a remedy for the inclination. This is true strength, to master one’s inclination, and through this one attains the joy of heart of those who seek Hashem. … Israel’s joy comes out of reverence.” This explains how Rabbah could judge his response. The joy in question arises through mastery of the inclination and reverence, so it can survive the loss of money.

paragraphs.text: Bava Batra 10a: "Rav Pappa was climbing a ladder when his foot slipped and he was about to fall (he ascended a ladder, his foot slipped, and he nearly fell). He became distressed and said: 'Were it so now, [euphemistically:] the one who hates us would have been held liable like Sabbath desecrators and like idolaters!' (He felt distressed and said: Had I fallen and died, that would have been like the penalty of stoning for Sabbath desecration or idolatry, so evidently Heaven has shown me that I sinned in one of these.) Chiyya bar Rav of Difti said to Rav Pappa: 'Perhaps a pauper came before you and you did not sustain him' (for charity is equal in weight to the prohibition of idolatry)."

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tehillim, Shocheir Tov 76:1 “‘Why did Yehudah merit kingship?’ ... When the students objected that Yehudah’s saving Yosef from being killed would suffice only to atone for his sale, Rabbi Tarfon answered that he merited kingship by leaping into the waves of the sea. ‘Yehudah became His sanctuary,’ and so Israel came under Yehudah’s rule.” The midrash discusses Yehudah’s conduct in Yosef’s sale and his descent into the sea together. Rav Tzadok develops this connection by reading the latter act as rectification.

paragraphs.text: Shemos Rabbah 42:3, on Bereishis 38:1 “When Yosef’s brothers sold him and could not comfort their father, they said: ‘Yehudah brought all this upon us. As we listened when he said not to kill Yosef, so we would have listened had he said not to sell him.’ They then put Yehudah under a ban. ‘Yehudah went down from his brothers’ signifies the lowering of his standing among them.” The midrash places particular responsibility for the sale on Yehudah, which underlies Rav Tzadok’s reading of Yehudah’s role at the sea. The Word body gives 42:2; in the Vilna division the account is 42:3.

paragraphs.text: Yerushalmi Sanhedrin 2:3 & Bavli Sanhedrin 25b: Yerushalmi Sanhedrin 2:3 states: "David said to his inclination: 'You craved something forbidden — Batsheva; by your life, I will make you crave in vain something permitted!'" These were the concubines whom Avshalom violated, who were halachically permitted to David, yet he separated from them in order to repent. And in Bavli Sanhedrin 25b it is explained that one who lends at interest is disqualified from giving testimony, and is considered to have repented only when he refrains from lending at interest even to a gentile. paragraphs.text: Bava Batra 12b & Responsa Rosh 97: Bava Batra 12b discusses a brother dividing an estate who wishes to receive in inheritance the field adjacent to his own existing field rather than receiving his inheritance by lot. According to Rabbah, we compel against the trait of Sodom (middat Sedom), and therefore we compel the brothers to give him the field adjacent to his own. According to Rav Yosef, we do not compel them, because the brothers can claim: "This plot of land is as choice and precious to us as the estates of the house of Bar Marion"; and the halachah follows Rav Yosef. Rabbeinu Tam explained that the family of Marion were wealthy and would not sell their lands except at a steep price. The Rosh, in his Responsa (Rule 97), challenges Rabbeinu Tam: According to his explanation, Rabbah's reasoning — that we compel against the trait of Sodom — is far more plausible, since the brothers have in fact agreed to cede the land to him and merely wish to profit financially from him! Therefore, the Rosh explains the Gemara in accordance with Rashi's commentary, and consequently rules like Rav Yosef just as the Gemara ruled; see there.

paragraphs.text: Sotah 47a: "'And the men of the city said to Elisha: Behold now, the site of the city is pleasant, as my lord sees, etc.' Now since the water was bad and the land caused bereavement, in what did its pleasantness consist? Rabbi Chanin said: The favor of a place in the eyes of its inhabitants (Rashi: even though it is bad, it appears pleasant to them). Rabbi Yochanan said: There are three kinds of favor: the favor of a place in the eyes of its inhabitants, the favor of a wife in the eyes of her husband, and the favor of a purchase in the eyes of its purchaser."

Rav Tzadok cites the idea in his own discussion of each person’s rooted connection to Eretz Yisrael.

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 8a: "It was taught in a Baraita: One who says, 'This sela is for charity in order that my son may live,' or 'in order that I may merit the World to Come,' behold, this person is a completely righteous individual (tzaddik gamur)." Rashi comments: "And we do not say that he is performing it not for its own sake (shelo lishmah); rather, he fulfilled the commandment of his Creator, Who commanded him to give charity, while also intending it for his own benefit." (That is to say, it is not purely lishmah, yet neither is it considered shelo lishmah.) Tosafot (8b, s.v. harei zeh) asks: "But did we not learn in the Mishnah: 'Be not like servants who serve the master for the sake of receiving a ration (pras)'? (And Tosafot answers:) That applies in a case where, if that benefit does not come to him, he regrets and second-guesses the charity he gave; however, one who does not regret or second-guess it — behold, he is a completely righteous individual."

paragraphs.text: Nedarim 62a: "It was taught in a Baraita: 'To love Hashem your God, to hearken to His voice, and to cleave to Him' (Devarim 30:20) — a person should not say: 'I will read Scripture so that they will call me a sage; I will study Mishnah so that they will call me Rabbi; I will master Talmudic traditions so that I will be an elder and sit in the academy.' Rather, study out of love, and honor will ultimately come, etc. Rabbi Eliezer bar Rabbi Tzadok says: Do matters for the sake of their Maker, and speak of them for their own sake; do not make them a crown with which to aggrandize yourself, and do not make them a spade with which to dig."

paragraphs.text: Bava Metzia 105b–106a: In the Mishnah on Bava Metzia 105b: "If one leases a field from his fellow and locusts devoured it or it was blasted by wind, if it is a regional blight, he may deduct from his fixed rental fee." In the Gemara (106a), they discuss a case where the tenant deviated from the agreement: if he sowed wheat instead of barley, the owner of the field cannot obligate him to pay the full rental fee by claiming that had he not deviated, the verse "You shall decree a matter and it will be fulfilled for you" (Iyov 22:28) would have been fulfilled for him. Further on, Shmuel says that if the tenant did not sow at all, he is liable for the full rental fee, because the owner can say to him: "Had you sown, the verse 'They shall not be ashamed in an evil time, and in days of famine they shall be satisfied' (Tehillim 37:19) would have been fulfilled." And Tosafot (106a, s.v. lenisa) explains that in Shmuel's case one cannot invoke "You shall decree a matter and it will be fulfilled for you," since they had not stipulated a specific crop, and it is specifically when one prays regarding a particular species that the Holy One, blessed be He, answers even without a miracle.

paragraphs.text: Ketubot 33b: Had they tortured Chananyah, Mishael, and Azaryah, they would have worshiped the image. Tosafot asks: Behold, there was Rabbi Akiva, whose flesh they combed with iron combs, and yet he said, "When will this verse of 'with all your soul' (Devarim 6:5) come to my hand so that I may fulfill it?" — meaning that the obligation of "with all your soul" applies even when they torture a person with severe torments like those endured by Rabbi Akiva. Rabbeinu Tam answers there that the image was not actual idolatry (avodah zarah), so by strict law they were not obligated to be killed rather than transgress; nevertheless, their self-sacrifice fulfilled the mitzvah of sanctifying God's Name (kiddush Hashem).

paragraphs.text: Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:7: "Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said: If someone were to say to me, 'Give your life for the sanctification of the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He,' I would give it — provided only that they kill me immediately; however, in the generation of religious persecution (shmad), I could not endure it. And what did they do in the generation of persecution? They would bring balls of iron, heat them white-hot in fire, and place them beneath their armpits, taking their lives thereby; and they would bring splinters of reeds and drive them beneath their fingernails, taking their lives thereby." And in Midrash Shochar Tov (Tehillim 16), the version of the text is shorter.

paragraphs.text: Avodah Zarah 4b: "And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Israel made the Golden Calf only in order to provide an opening of encouragement for penitents (ba'alei teshuvah), as it is stated: 'O that they had such a heart as this always, to fear Me all the days, etc.' (Devarim 5:26). And this accords with what Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai: Neither was David suited for that deed, nor was Israel suited for that deed. David was not suited for that deed (concerning Batsheva), as it is written: 'And my heart is slain within me' (Tehillim 109:22). And Israel was not suited for that deed, as it is written: 'O that they had such a heart as this always, to fear Me all the days.'"

paragraphs.text: Bava Metzia 106a: "If a shepherd was tending his flock and left his flock (unguarded) and entered the town, and a wolf came and tore an animal, or a lion came and mauled one, we do not automatically say: 'Had he been there, he would have saved it'; rather, we assess him: if he (the shepherd) would have been able to save it, he is liable, and if not, he is exempt." And the Gemara asks: Yet could the owner not claim, "Had you been there, perhaps you would have succeeded miraculously in protecting my flock, just like David who struck down the lion and the bear"? And the Gemara answers that the shepherd can reply to the owner: "Had you been worthy of a miracle, a miracle would have occurred even without me, like the goats of Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa that brought bears back on their horns"—meaning that against any person one can argue: you yourself could have been worthy of a miracle.

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 53b: "The Sages taught: There was once an incident involving a certain man whose wife died and left him a nursing infant son, and he did not have the wages of a wet nurse to pay. A miracle was performed for him, and breasts opened up for him like the two breasts of a woman, and he nursed his son. Rav Yosef said: 'Come and see how great this man is, that such a miracle was performed for him!' Abaye said to him: 'On the contrary, how inferior this man is, that the orders of Creation had to be altered for him!'"

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 25b: "The Sages taught: Who is wealthy? Anyone who takes contentment in his wealth; these are the words of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Tarfon says: Anyone who possesses a hundred vineyards, a hundred fields, and a hundred servants working in them. Rabbi Akiva says: Anyone who has a wife comely in her deeds. Rabbi Yose says: Anyone who has a privy near his table." And Rashi explained that the practical difference is that one should exert oneself until reaching that measure of wealth, and neither exert oneself more nor less.

paragraphs.text: Nedarim 41a: "'In lack of everything' (Deuteronomy 28:48)—Rabbi Ami said in the name of Rav: Without a lamp and without a table. Rav Chisda said: Without a wife... Rav Nachman said: Without knowledge (da'at)... Abaye said: We hold a tradition that there is no poor person except one who is poor in knowledge. In the West (the Land of Israel) they say: One who has this within him has everything within him. (Rashi: One who possesses knowledge is like one who possesses everything, for he lacks nothing.) One who does not have this within him, what does he have within him? One who has acquired this, what does he lack? One who has not acquired this, what has he acquired?"

paragraphs.text: Eruvin 45a: We derive from King David that one risks one's life and desecrates the Shabbat to wage war even against enemies who have come merely to plunder straw and stubble from border settlements, "as it is written: 'And they told David, saying: Behold, the Philistines are fighting against Keilah, and they are plundering the threshing floors' (I Samuel 23:1). A Tanna taught: Keilah was a town near the border, and they came only over matters of straw and stubble, etc.; and it is written: 'And David inquired of Hashem, saying: Shall I go and strike these Philistines? And Hashem said to David: Go and strike the Philistines, and save Keilah' (I Samuel 23:2)." The intent of his inquiry via the Urim veTumim was whether he would prevail or not, and he was informed that he would prevail. Even so, it is considered that he risked his life, because he was ready to give up his life.

paragraphs.text: Bava Metzia 42a: "The Sages taught: One who goes to measure his threshing floor says: 'May it be Your will, Hashem our God, that You send blessing into the work of our hands.' Once he begins to measure, he says: 'Blessed is He Who sends blessing into this heap.' If he measured and afterward recited the blessing, behold, this is a vain prayer, because blessing is not found in something weighed, nor in something measured, nor in something counted, but only in something hidden from the eye, as it is stated: 'Hashem will command the blessing to be with you in your storehouses' (Deuteronomy 28:8)."

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 7a: "It was taught in a Baraita: Rabbi Yishmael ben Elisha said: Once I entered the innermost sanctum (the Holy of Holies) to offer the incense, and I saw Akathriel Yah, Hashem of Hosts, seated upon a high and exalted throne. And He said to me: 'Yishmael, My son, bless Me!' I said to Him: 'May it be Your will that Your mercy overcome Your anger, that Your mercy prevail over Your strict attributes, that You conduct Yourself toward Your children with the attribute of mercy, and that You act toward them beyond the strict letter of the law.' And He nodded His head to me. And this teaches us that the blessing of an ordinary person should not be light in your eyes."

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 102a: "Rabbi Yitzchak said: There is not a single retribution that comes upon the world that does not contain one twenty-fourth of the tipping of the scale of a litra from the first Golden Calf (meaning that the sin of the Golden Calf joins in and tips the scale toward liability), as it is stated: 'And on the day when I visit, I will visit their sin upon them' (Exodus 32:34). Rabbi Chanina said: After twenty-four generations this verse was collected, as it is stated: 'And He called in my ears with a loud voice, saying: Approach, you who have charge over the punishment of the city, every man with his weapon of destruction in his hand' (Ezekiel 9:1)." Rashi: "And from the incident of the Golden Calf until Tzidkiyahu there were twenty-four generations."

paragraphs.text: Horayot 6a: "Rav Pappa said: When we learned the oral tradition that a sin-offering whose owner died must be left to die, that applies only to an individual, not to a community, because there is no death for a community. From where does Rav Pappa derive this? If we say from what is written: 'In place of your fathers shall be your sons' (Psalms 45:17)—if so, even regarding an individual too [the same should apply]? ... Rather, since it effects atonement for the living (since the communal sin-offering atones for the living members), it also effects atonement for the dead." (It atones for the deceased as well, and this is the meaning of "there is no death for a community," because part of it is always alive.)

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 110b: According to the view of Rabbi Akiva, the Generation of the Wilderness has no share in the World to Come, and regarding this, "Rabbah bar bar Chanah said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: Rabbi Akiva abandoned his characteristic lovingkindness, as it is stated: 'Go and proclaim in the ears of Jerusalem, saying: I remember in your favor the devotion of your youth, your love as a bride, how you followed Me in the wilderness, in an unsown land' (Jeremiah 2:2)—now if others enter (the World to Come) through their merit, how much more so they themselves?!"

paragraphs.text: Bava Metzia 96b / Takanat Usha: The discussion concerns the Enactment of Usha: "If a woman sold her usufruct (melog) property during her husband's lifetime and then died, the husband extracts the property from the buyers." Rami bar Chama asked: If property that had been consecrated to Heaven fell to one's wife as an inheritance without the heirs knowing this, who is guilty of misappropriation of consecrated property (me'ilah)? And the Gemara raises the possibility that perhaps the court itself would be guilty of misappropriation, since it is the court that transfers ownership of the consecrated property to the husband by force of its enactment, thereby removing it into mundane status.

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 10b: "Rabbi Yitzchak said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan, who said in the name of Rabbi Yose bar Rabbi Chanina in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov: Whoever eats and drinks and afterward prays — concerning him Scripture states: 'And Me you have cast behind your back (gavekha)' (Melakhim I 14:9). Do not read 'your back (gavekha),' but rather 'your haughtiness (ge'ekha).' Said the Holy One, blessed be He: 'After this one has exalted himself, he now accepts upon himself the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven!'"

paragraphs.text: Bava Batra 16b: "A daughter was born to Rabbi Shimon the son of Rebbi (a daughter was born to him), and his mind grew faint (he became saddened). His father said to him: 'Increase has come to the world!' Bar Kappara said to him: 'Your father has comforted you with vain consolations! For it was taught in a Baraita: It is impossible for the world to exist without males and without females; yet fortunate is he whose children are males, and woe to him whose children are females.' ... This follows a dispute of Tannaim: 'And Hashem blessed Avraham with everything (ba-kol)' (Bereishit 24:1) — what does 'with everything' mean? Rabbi Meir says: That he did not have a daughter. Rabbi Yehudah says: That he had a daughter."

paragraphs.text: Bava Batra 141a: From the wording of the Mishnah: "If one says: 'If my wife bears a male, he shall take a maneh (one hundred zuz); if a female, two hundred zuz.'" (The Gemara infers:) Is this to say that a daughter is preferable to him? (The Gemara objects to this from the laws of inheritance, where a son takes precedence, and answers:) "With regard to inheritance, a son is preferable; with regard to generous maintenance, his daughter is preferable to him. And Shmuel said: Here we are dealing with a woman giving birth for the first time (a firstborn child), in accordance with Rav Chisda; for Rav Chisda said: 'A daughter first is a good omen for sons.' Some say: Because she helps raise her brothers (she brings up her brothers). And others say: Because the evil eye has no sway over him. Rav Chisda said: 'And as for me, my daughters are dearer to me than my sons.' And if you wish, say: Whose view does this Mishnah follow? Rabbi Yehudah" (as cited above). Rashi explained: "Some explain Rav Chisda's statement as referring to a woman giving birth for the first time, like our sugya, yet the wording, inasmuch as he says 'as for me (le-didi),' does not indicate this. Rather, it appears in my eyes that his sons did not survive, only his daughters, and therefore he longed for daughters — though Rav Chisda's view has still not settled satisfactorily in my mind." Tosafot: "This explanation does not appear tenable, for he had many sons (as we find in several places throughout the Talmud). Rather, it appears to Rabbeinu Yitzchak that the reason he said 'my daughters are dearer to me than my sons' was because his sons-in-law were the greatest sages of the generation — Rava and Mar Ukva bar Chama."

Rather, it appears in my eyes that his sons did not survive, only his daughters, and therefore he longed for daughters — though Rav Chisda's view has still not settled satisfactorily in my mind." Tosafot: "This explanation does not appear tenable, for he had many sons (as we find in several places throughout the Talmud). Rather, it appears to Rabbeinu Yitzchak that the reason he said 'my daughters are dearer to me than my sons' was because his sons-in-law were the greatest sages of the generation — Rava and Mar Ukva bar Chama."

paragraphs.text: Yoma 72b: "Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: What is the meaning of that which is written: 'Why is there money in the hand of a fool to purchase wisdom, when he has no heart?' (Mishlei 17:16)? Woe to the enemies of Torah scholars (a euphemism for the scholars themselves) who engage in Torah study yet possess no fear of Heaven!" And fear of Heaven stems from the recognition of one's own lack.

paragraphs.text: Niddah 16b: "Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa expounded: That angel who is appointed over conception is named Lailah, and he takes the seminal drop, sets it before the Holy One, blessed be He, and says before Him: 'Master of the Universe, what shall become of this drop—mighty or weak? Wise or foolish? Rich or poor?' Yet he does not say 'wicked or righteous,' in accordance with the statement of Rabbi Chanina; for Rabbi Chanina said: Everything is in the hands of Heaven except for the fear of Heaven, as it is stated: 'And now, O Israel, what does Hashem your God ask of you, if not to fear, etc.'"

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 31a–b: "Rabbah bar Rav Huna said: Any person who possesses Torah without fear of Heaven is comparable to a treasurer to whom they handed the inner keys, while the outer keys they did not hand to him—through which entrance can he enter? Rabbi Yannai proclaimed: Woe to one who has no courtyard-dwelling (darta), yet constructs a gateway (tar'a) for a courtyard-dwelling!" (Meaning: Woe to one who has no dwelling, yet makes a gate for a dwelling.)

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 31a: "Even so (even though he studied Torah), if 'the fear of Hashem is his treasure'—yes; if not—no. This is comparable to a man who said to his agent: 'Bring up a kor of wheat for me to the upper loft.' He went and brought it up for him. The master asked him: 'Did you mix a kav of chumton into it for me?' He replied: 'No.' The master said to him: 'It would have been better had you not brought it up.'" For without the chumton, which is a small measure of preservative earth, the wheat does not keep; and likewise, without fear of Heaven, the Torah is of no enduring account.

paragraphs.text: Yevamot 45a: "People say: 'In Media, a camel dances on a kav.'" This is a marvel and an exaggeration, saying that in the kingdom of Media a camel dances with all four of its legs upon a small kav-measure. Ketubot 62b: "A woman prefers one kav with marital intimacy over ten kabin with abstinence."

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 33a: "For the sin of bloodshed, the Beis HaMikdash is destroyed and the Shekhinah departs from Israel, as it is stated: 'You shall not pollute, etc., and you shall not defile the Land in which you dwell, in the midst of which I dwell'—implying that if you defile it, you shall not dwell in it and I will not dwell in its midst. For the sins of forbidden sexual relations, idolatry, and the neglect of Shemittah and Yovel years, exile comes to the world: they are exiled, and others come and settle in their place, as it is stated: '...that the Land not vomit you out when you defile it.'"

Meforshei HaShas: Rashi on Bava Kamma 12b:12:1 — “ואיתיביה - גרסי': שהן ממונו - אפי' בזמן שבית המקדש קיים דהא קרא דשבועת הפקדון בזמן שבית המקדש הוא דמחייב ליה אשם:”. Mishnah: Mishnah Nazir 5:4 — “… נזירים מן הגולה ומצאו בית המקדש חרב, אמר להם נחום המדי, אלו הייתם יודעים שבית המקדש חרב הייתם נוזרים. אמרו לו לא, …”. paragraphs.text: Rabbi Nachman of Breslov, Likutei Moharan II 78, urges someone at the lowest spiritual level to call out like Jonah from the depths and hold on to whatever service remains possible. In II 112:1 he applies the same principle to wrongdoing itself: the possibility of causing damage entails the possibility of repair. Both passages illuminate Rav Tzadok’s refusal to equate a person’s present condition with the limits of repentance.

paragraphs.text: Tanchuma Vayera 16: "'Who says of Jerusalem: It shall be inhabited, and of the cities of Judah: They shall be built.' Now what connection does this verse have here? Rather, it comes to teach you that even though people have despaired of her and one has come setting a limit declaring that she will never be rebuilt, she will indeed be rebuilt, as it is stated: 'Who says of Jerusalem: It shall be inhabited,' and it is written: 'For Hashem has built Zion.' And if you are astonished at this, 'Look to Avraham your father and to Sarah who bore you': just as I did for Avraham and Sarah, so will I do for Jerusalem."

paragraphs.text: Sukkah 31a: "A certain elderly woman (Rashi: from whom the servants of the Exilarch had stolen wood and used it as sukkah roofing) came before Rav Nachman and said to him: 'The Exilarch and all the rabbis of the Exilarch's household are sitting in a stolen sukkah (and are not fulfilling their obligation)!' She cried out, but Rav Nachman paid her no heed. She said to him: 'A woman whose father (Avraham our father) had three hundred and eighteen servants cries out before you, and you pay her no heed?!' Rav Nachman said concerning her: 'This one is a noisy shouter, and she is entitled only to the monetary value of the wood.'" For on account of the rabbinic enactment to facilitate penitents (takanat ha-shavim), the Sages ordained that the stolen wood becomes the property of the robber, and he is obligated to return only the monetary value of the wood and not the wood itself.

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 88a: A certain Sadducee said to Rava: "'An impetuous people, who placed your mouths before your ears (you are a hasty nation, for you put your mouths ahead of your ears)... First you should have listened: if you were able, you should have accepted it, and if not, you should not have accepted it (at the outset you ought to have heard the commandments of the Torah; if you could fulfill them, you would accept them, and if not, you would not accept them).'"

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 17a: "Rabbi Alexandri, after praying, would say the following: 'Master of the Universe, it is revealed and known before You that our will is to perform Your will, and what prevents us? The leaven in the dough (the evil inclination) and subjugation to foreign kingdoms. May it be Your will to rescue us from their hand, so that we may return to fulfill the statutes of Your will with a whole heart.'"

paragraphs.text: Leviticus 23:17 explicitly requires the two loaves to be baked leavened. Mishnah Menachot 5:1 sets those loaves and the leavened bread of the thanksgiving offering apart from grain offerings generally, then debates how their starter is prepared. The legal exception gives force to Rav Tzadok’s image of redirecting the leavening impulse itself toward divine service.

paragraphs.text: Yevamot 77a: "Rava expounded: What is the meaning of that which is written, 'You have loosened my bonds'? David said before the Holy One, blessed be He: 'Master of the Universe, two bonds that rested upon me You have loosened: Ruth the Moabitess and Naamah the Ammonitess.' Rava further expounded: What is the meaning of that which is written, 'Many things have You done, Hashem my God, Your wonders and Your thoughts toward us'? It does not state 'toward me,' but rather 'toward us,' teaching that Rechavam was sitting in David's lap, and he (David) said to him: 'Concerning me and concerning you were these two verses stated.'" That is, a Moabite woman and an Ammonite woman are permitted to convert and marry into the congregation, even though a Moabite man and an Ammonite man may not.

paragraphs.text: Yerushalmi Kiddushin 3:12: "Rabbi Yannai in the name of Rebbe: If an idolater or a slave cohabited with a Jewish woman, the child is a mamzer. Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha, Rabbi Shimon bar Abba, and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi in the name of Rabban Gamliel the son of Rebbe: The child is neither wholly fit nor disqualified as a mamzer, but rather tainted (meaning if she bore a daughter, that daughter is disqualified from marrying into the priesthood). Rabbi Yonatan went up with Rabbi Yudah Nesi'ah to Chamta of Gader, and he ruled there: The child is fit. Rabbi Ze'ira said: This child, the further along he goes, the higher he rises. (Korban HaEdah: This child of an idolater or slave, as each generation progresses, rises and becomes more esteemed; for Rebbe said that the child is a mamzer, Rabban Gamliel his son said that he is merely tainted, and Rabbi Yudah HaNasi his grandson said that he is completely fit.)"

paragraphs.text: Sukkah 52a: It is recounted that Abaye heard a certain man saying to a woman who was not his wife, "Come, let us set out early to walk along our road." Abaye said, "I will follow after them in order to keep them away from transgression," and he followed after them for three parsaos. When they parted from one another, he heard them say, "Our road is long and our company has been pleasant," and thus they parted without any suspicion of sin. "Abaye said: Had it been the one who hates me, he would not have been able to restrain himself" — meaning, if my enemy — my evil inclination — had been secluded with the woman, he would not have been able to overcome it and would have sinned; and he said this euphemistically regarding himself. "He went and leaned himself against the bolt of the doorway and was distressed" — he leaned upon the bolt of the door and grieved over his evil inclination, which was stronger than the evil inclination of that man. "A certain elder came and taught him: Whoever is greater than his fellow, his evil inclination is greater than his."

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 102a: When Achiyah HaShiloni met Yeravam, he found him wrapped in a new garment, regarding which Rav Nachman explains: "The Torah scholarship of Yeravam had no flaw whatsoever... and they innovated matters that no ear had ever heard." "The two of them were alone in the field... meaning that all Torah scholars were comparable before them to the grass of the field. And there are those who say: that all the reasons of the Torah were revealed to them like an open field." And there, the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Yeravam: "Repent, and I, and you, and the son of Yishai will stroll in Gan Eden..." And there on side b (102b), Menasheh proved to Rav Ashi that his stature in Torah was great. And there on 103b: "The Rabbis taught: Menasheh used to expound fifty-five facets in Toras Kohanim, corresponding to the years of his reign; Achav — eighty-five; Yeravam — one hundred and three." And there on 106b concerning Doeg: "And Rabbi Yitzchak said: What is the meaning of that which is written, 'Where is the one who counts, where is the one who weighs, where is the one who counts the towers?' 'Where is the one who counts' — who counted all the letters in the Torah; 'where is the one who weighs' — who weighed all the lenient and stringent inferences in the Torah; 'where is the one who counts the towers' — who used to count three hundred decided halachos concerning a 'tower flying in the air.' Rebbi said: Doeg and Achitofel raised four hundred halachic inquiries concerning a 'tower flying in the air.'" And regarding these five — Yeravam, Menasheh, Achav, Doeg, and Achitofel — the Sages stated that they have no share in the World to Come. And there are two more who were enumerated in the Mishnah on 90a, namely Geichazi and Bilaam.

paragraphs.text: Chagigah 15a: "He ('Acher' to Rabbi Meir) said to him: Rabbi Akiva your teacher... expounded thus:... He created the righteous and He created the wicked; He created Gan Eden and He created Gehinnom. Every single individual has two portions, one in Gan Eden and one in Gehinnom. If a righteous person merits, he takes his own portion and the portion of his fellow in Gan Eden; if a wicked person is found guilty, he takes his own portion and the portion of his fellow in Gehinnom."

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 99b: "She (Timna) wished to convert; she came before Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov, and they did not accept her. She went and became a concubine to Eliphaz the son of Esav. She said: 'Better that she be a maidservant to this nation (for they fear Heaven — Rashi), rather than be a noblewoman to another nation.' From her came forth Amalek, who afflicted Israel. What is the reason? Because they ought not to have pushed her away."

paragraphs.text: Parallels. Halachah: Sefer HaChinukh 528:1 — “שלא להחיות נשמה משבעה עממין – שהזהרנו בלא תעשה שלא נחיה אחד משבעה עממים בכל מקום שנמצאם ונוכל להרגם בלי סכנה לנפשותינו. …”. Talmud Bavli: Makkos 8a — “אמר רב פפא: לא צריכא אלא לאשפה העשויה ליפנות בה בלילה, ואין עשויה ליפנות בה ביום, ואיכא דמקרי ויתיב. פושע לא הוי …”. Meforshei HaShas: Tosafos on Makkot 8a:9:1-2 — “… דלית ליה לאסוקי אדעתיה הוא דמקרי ויתיב כיון שאינה עשויה ליפנות כלל אבל השתא בעשויה ליפנות בלילה אית ליה לאסוקי גם ביום …”. Talmud Yerushalmi: Jerusalem Talmud Sheviit 6:4 — “… לארץ לארץ. אמר רבי שמעתי בפירוש שמוציאין מסוריה ואין מביאין מחוצה לארץ. הלכה: בראשונה היה הירק אסור בספרי ארץ ישראל התקינו שיהא …”. Meforshei HaYerushalmi: Penei Moshe on Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim 2:4 — “… המזבח וכמדרשו של יהוידע הכהן שנשנה לקמן סוף פרק ששי. ובדפוס משנה דהכא כתיב חולין ונוסחא אחריתא היא וכן משמע לעיל בהלכה …”. Ran on Nedarim 62a comments: "'Perform matters for the sake of their Maker (po'olam)' — for the sake of the Holy One, blessed be He, who made them and commanded concerning them." The Rosh there does not comment on this phrase at all; apparently an error crept in and the intended reference is to Rashi, who explains: "'Their Maker (po'olam)' — for the sake of Heaven."

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah 4a: In Rosh Hashanah 4a, the Gemara states that King Cyrus soured and acted wickedly, and that the offerings he sent to the Temple were for his own benefit (so that they would pray on his behalf). The Gemara asks: "Was it not taught in a baraita: One who says, 'This sela is for charity so that my sons may live and so that through it I may merit the life of the World to Come,' behold, this person is completely righteous? There is no difficulty: here it speaks of an Israelite (who is completely righteous), whereas there it speaks of an idolater." Rashi explains: "'Here it speaks of an Israelite' — whose heart is devoted to Heaven, so that if misfortune befalls him in his lifetime he does not protest in grievance, but attributes the suffering to his own iniquity. An idolater, however, protests in grievance (against Hashem, may He be blessed) if he is not treated well in accordance with his deed."

paragraphs.text: Rambam, Hilkhot Gerushin 2:20: "When the law dictates that a man is to be compelled to divorce his wife and he refuses to divorce her, a Jewish court in every place and at every time administers lashes to him until he declares, 'I am willing,' and writes the get, and it is a valid get... Why is this get not void on the grounds that he acted under duress?... Because we do not apply the category of duress except to someone who is pressured and forced to do something he is not obligated by the Torah to do — such as someone beaten until he sold or gifted property. However, one whose evil inclination overpowered him to neglect a mitzvah or commit a transgression, and who was beaten until he performed what he was obligated to do or distanced himself from what he was forbidden to do, is not considered coerced by others; rather, he coerced himself through his own evil mindset. Therefore, this man who refuses to divorce, inasmuch as he wishes to remain part of Israel, truly wishes to fulfill all the mitzvot and distance himself from transgressions, and it is only his evil inclination that overpowered him; once he is beaten until his inclination weakens and he declares, 'I am willing,' he has divorced of his own free will."

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 6a: "What is the meaning of 'and for those who esteem His Name' (Malakhi 3:16)? Rav Ashi said: Even if a person intended to perform a mitzvah and was prevented by circumstances beyond his control and did not perform it, Scripture credits him as though he had performed it." The same teaching appears in Shabbat 63a. Our Master (Rav Tzadok) introduces the novel insight that even if the thought to perform the mitzvah was not for the sake of Heaven, even then Scripture credits him as though he had performed it.

paragraphs.text: Arakhin 16b: "Rav Yehudah the son of Rabbi Shimon inquired of him: Between rebuke delivered for its own sake and humility practiced not for its own sake, which of them is preferable? (Rashi: Rebuke for the sake of Heaven, or humility not for its own sake — where one acts humbly by refraining from rebuking someone for his sins, and that humility is not for the sake of Heaven, but rather so that the other will not hate him — which is preferable?) He replied to him: Do you not concede that humility for its own sake is preferable (to both humility not for its own sake and rebuke for its own sake), as the Master said: Humility is the greatest of all virtues? (He answered him:) Humility practiced not for its own sake is likewise preferable, for Rav Yehudah said in the name of Rav: A person should always engage in Torah and mitzvot even if not for their own sake, because from doing so not for their own sake he comes to do so for their own sake."

paragraphs.text: Ruth Rabbah 5:6: "Rabbi Yitzchak bar Marion said: Scripture comes to teach you that if a person performs a mitzvah, he should perform it with a whole heart. For had Reuven known that the Holy One, blessed be He, would write about him, 'And Reuven heard and rescued him from their hand' (Bereshit 37:21), he would have carried him on his shoulder back to his father; had Aharon known that the Holy One, blessed be He, would write about him, 'Behold, he is going out to meet you' (Shemot 4:14), he would have gone out to greet him with timbrels and dances; and had Boaz known that the Holy One, blessed be He, would write about him, 'And he handed her parched grain, and she ate and was satisfied and left some over' (Ruth 2:14), he would have fed her fattened calves."

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 20a (Boaz vs. Palti ben Laish): Boaz's trial when Ruth came to the threshing floor and lay at his feet was indeed a one-time event, though both of them were unmarried. By contrast, the trial of Palti ben Laish lasted the entire time he was married to Mikhal, and according to the ruling of Shaul's court their marriage was valid and he was halakhically obligated in her conjugal rights.

paragraphs.text: Vayikra Rabbah 32:4–5: It is recounted there that the mother of the Israelite who blasphemed had relations with an Egyptian man, and from that union the blasphemer was born, as it is stated: "And the son of an Israelite woman went out, and he was the son of an Egyptian man" (Vayikra 24:10). The mother's name was Shelomit bat Dibri, because she used to greet everyone ("Shalom") with loose familiarity and idle chatter. She likewise greeted the Egyptian taskmaster appointed over her husband and smiled before him, leading the Egyptian to think he could seduce her into immorality; he dispatched her husband to labor and violated his wife by force, and that very Egyptian was the one whom Moshe slew.

paragraphs.text: Chullin 56b & Shemot Rabbah 37:1: Chullin 56b: "It was taught in a Baraita: Rabbi Meir used to say: 'He made you and established you' refers to a city that contains everything within itself: from him come its priests, from him its prophets, from him its officers, from him its kings, as it is stated: 'From him comes the cornerstone, from him the tent peg, etc.'" Shemot Rabbah 37:1: "'And you, bring near to yourself Aharon your brother.' This is the meaning of what is written: 'From him comes the cornerstone, from him the tent peg, from him the bow of battle.' Come and see: when the ancient nations sought to appoint a king over themselves, they would bring someone from anywhere and appoint him over themselves... But Israel is not so; rather, from them come their great leaders, from them their kings, from them their priests, from them their prophets, from them their officers, as it is stated, etc."

Come and see: when the ancient nations sought to appoint a king over themselves, they would bring someone from anywhere and appoint him over themselves... But Israel is not so; rather, from them come their great leaders, from them their kings, from them their priests, from them their prophets, from them their officers, as it is stated, etc."

paragraphs.text: Sukkah 52b: "The academy of Rabbi Yishmael taught: If this repulsive one encounters you, drag him to the study hall: if he is of stone, he will dissolve; if he is of iron, he will shatter. If he is of stone, he will dissolve, as it is written: 'Ho, all who are thirsty, go to the water,' and it is written: 'Water wears away stones.' If he is of iron, he will shatter, as it is written: 'Behold, My word is like fire, declares Hashem, and like a hammer that shatters rock.'"

paragraphs.text: Chagigah 27a & Tosafot: Chagigah 27a: "Rabbi Abbahu said in the name of Rabbi Elazar: The fire of Gehinnom has no power over Torah scholars, by an a fortiori inference from the salamander: if regarding the salamander, which is merely an offspring of fire, fire has no power over one who smears himself with its blood, how much more so Torah scholars, whose entire body is fire, as it is written: 'Behold, My word is like fire, declares Hashem'! Reish Lakish said: The fire of Gehinnom has no power over the transgressors of Israel, by an a fortiori inference from the Golden Altar: if regarding the Golden Altar, upon which there was only a plating as thick as a gold dinar, fire had no power over it for so many years, how much more so the transgressors of Israel, who are as full of mitzvot as a pomegranate is full of seeds, as it is written: 'Your temples (rakatekh) are like a slice of pomegranate': do not read rakatekh ('your temples'), rather reikanin shebakh ('the empty ones among you')!" And in Tosafot there, s.v. She'ein bo ela ovi dinar: "In the Midrash Tanchuma it is stated that Moshe wondered about this: 'Is it possible that the wood will not burn?!' And the Omnipresent said to him: 'Such is My way with supernal fire: fire consumes fire and does not destroy,' as it is written: 'and the bush was not consumed.'"

paragraphs.text: Bava Batra 78b: "Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: What is the meaning of what is written: 'Therefore the moshlim say, etc.'? 'The moshlim': these are those who rule (moshlim) over their inclination. 'Come to Heshbon': come and let us reckon the accounting (cheshbon) of the world, weighing the loss incurred by a mitzvah against its reward, and the reward of a transgression against its loss. 'Let it be built and established': if you do so, you will be built up in This World and established for the World to Come. 'City of Sichon': if a person makes himself like a young donkey (ayir) that follows after pleasant coaxing (sichah na'ah), what is written afterward? 'For a fire went forth from Heshbon, etc.': a fire shall go forth from those who make this reckoning (mechashvin) and consume those who do not make this reckoning..."

Re'uyin halalu: "He derives this from the end of the verse, as it is written: 'And the spirit of God came upon him.'"

paragraphs.text: Vayikra Rabbah 4:6: "Chizkiyah taught: 'Israel is a scattered sheep': Israel is compared to a sheep; just as when this sheep is struck on its head or on one of its limbs, all of its limbs feel it, so too are Israel: when one of them sins, all of them feel it, as it is written, 'Shall one man sin...' Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai taught: This may be compared to people sitting in a ship; one of them took a drill and began drilling beneath himself. His companions said to him: 'What are you sitting and doing?' He said to them: 'What concern is it of yours? Am I not drilling beneath myself?' They said to him: 'Because the water will rise and flood the ship upon us!'"

paragraphs.text: Yechezkel 3:17–21: "Son of man, I have appointed you a watchman for the House of Israel; when you hear a word from My mouth, you shall warn them from Me. When I say to the wicked man, 'You shall surely die,' and you do not warn him, nor do you speak to warn the wicked man from his wicked way so that he may live, that wicked man shall die in his iniquity, and his blood I will demand from your hand. Yet if you have warned the wicked man, and he does not turn back from his wickedness and from his wicked way, he shall die in his iniquity, while you have delivered your soul. And when a righteous man turns away from his righteousness and commits injustice, and I place a stumbling block before him, he shall die; because you did not warn him, he shall die in his sin, and his righteous deeds that he performed shall not be remembered, and his blood I will demand from your hand. Yet if you have warned the righteous man so that the righteous man does not sin, and he did not sin, he shall surely live because he heeded the warning, and you have delivered your soul."

paragraphs.text: Parallels. Halachah: Aruch HaShulchan, Yoreh De'ah 246:10 — “וכך שנינו בתורת כהנים פרשת בחקתי: "ואם לא תשמעו לי, ולא תעשו את כל המצות האלה" – וכי יש לך אדם שאינו …”. Meforshei HaMishnah: Bartenura on Mishnah Sotah 1:9 — “וכן לענין הטובה. נותנים לו לאדם שכר מעין הטובה שעשה. ומיהו יותר ממה שעשה משתלם, דמדה טובה מרבה בתשלומין ממדת פרענות:”. Meforshei Tanach: Ohel Ya'akov on Torah, Bechukotai 8:1 — “… ואם לא תשמעו לי שיודע את רבונו ומתכוין למרוד בו יש לך אדם שאינו לומד ואינו עושה אבל אינו מואס באחרים העושין …”. paragraphs.text: Sotah 5a: "Rabbi Chiyya bar Ashi said in the name of Rav: A Torah scholar must possess one-eighth of an eighth." And further on: "Rava said: Under a ban be the one who has it, and under a ban be the one who does not have it." Rashi explains: "'One-eighth of an eighth': It is a tiny measure, namely an uchla; meaning he must possess a slight measure of pride so that frivolous people will not treat him lightly, and so that his words will be accepted upon them even against their will. 'Under a ban be the one who has it': (Let anyone be under excommunication who possesses) arrogance of spirit. 'And under a ban be the one who does not have it': Even a small measure of pride, because the people of his town will not revere him and he will lack the strength to rebuke them."

paragraphs.text: Horayot 13b: In Horayot 13b it is recounted that initially people were accustomed to rise equally before Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel the Nasi (Patriarch), Rabbi Meir the Chacham (Sage), and Rabbi Natan the Av Beit Din (Head of the Rabbinical Court). Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel considered it proper to enact a distinction between the honor of the Nasi and the honor of the Chacham and the Av Beit Din. He therefore instituted that in honor of a Nasi who enters, everyone stands; in honor of an Av Beit Din, only the row past which he walks stands; and in honor of a Chacham, each time only the individual person past whom the Chacham walks stands. When Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Natan saw this, they sought to embarrass him before everyone by raising questions in Tractate Uktzin that he would not know how to answer, thereby removing him from his post. Through a student who hinted to him that they intended to do this on the morrow, he reviewed the tractate thoroughly, knew how to answer, and afterward ordered their expulsion from the study hall. After a great need arose for their assistance in the Torah study of the study hall, Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel ordered that teachings should not be cited in their names; rather, Rabbi Natan's words would be cited in the name of "Some say" (Yesh Omrim), and Rabbi Meir's words in the name of "Others" (Acherim). Afterward, Rabbi Natan went and appeased Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, and they resumed citing teachings in his name.

paragraphs.text: Bereishit Rabbah 32:3: "Rabbi Yonatan said: A potter does not examine defective jars, for he cannot tap them even once before he breaks them. Which ones does he examine? Sound jars; even if he taps them several times, they do not break. Similarly, the Holy One, blessed be He, does not test the wicked, but rather the righteous, as it is stated: 'Hashem tests the righteous' (Psalms 11:5)."

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 107a: "He (David) said before Him: Master of the Universe, why do people say 'the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob,' and do not say 'the God of David'? He replied: They were tested by Me, whereas you have not been tested by Me. He said before Him: Master of the Universe, examine me and test me! As it is stated: 'Examine me, Hashem, and test me, etc.' (Psalms 26:2)."

paragraphs.text: Bereishit Rabbah 8:5: "Rabbi Simon said: At the time when the Holy One, blessed be He, came to create Adam the first man... Kindness said: Let him be created, for he bestows acts of kindness; Truth said: Let him not be created, for he is entirely falsehoods; Righteousness said: Let him be created, for he performs righteous deeds; Peace said: Let him not be created, for he is entirely strife. What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He took Truth and cast it to the ground; that is what is written: 'And it cast truth to the ground' (Daniel 8:12)."

paragraphs.text: Gittin 56b–57a: The Gemara recounts the story of Titus the Wicked, who destroyed the Holy Temple and was afterward punished by a gnat pecking at his brain, and who requested that after his death his ashes be scattered across seven seas so that he could not be brought to judgment on high. Onkelos, his sister's son, wished to convert; he raised Titus through necromancy and asked him: Who is esteemed in the World of Truth? Titus answered him: Israel. He asked him: Is it worthwhile to cleave to them? He answered him: Their decrees are numerous and impossible to fulfill; rather, whoever torments them in this world becomes a chief. He asked him: What is your punishment? He answered him: That which I decreed upon myself: every day they gather my ashes and scatter them across seven seas... He then went and raised "that man" (Oto HaIsh) through necromancy and asked him: Who is esteemed in the World of Truth? He answered him: Israel. He asked him: Should one cleave to them? He answered him: Seek their welfare and do not seek their harm; whoever touches them is as though touching the pupil of the eye of the Holy One, blessed be He. He asked him: What is your punishment? He told him: In boiling excrement... Come and see the difference between the transgressors of Israel and the prophets of the nations of the world who worship idolatry!

paragraphs.text: Targum Yonatan, Vayechi 50:13 (free Hebrew rendering): And the sons of Jacob carried him to the land of Canaan. Once Esau the Wicked heard this, he set out from Mount Gabla, came to Hebron, and did not permit Joseph to bury his father in the Cave of Machpelah. Immediately Naphtali ran, went down to Egypt, returned that very day, and brought the deed that Esau had written for his brother Jacob regarding his portion in the Cave of Machpelah. Immediately Joseph signaled to Chushim son of Dan, who took a sword and severed Esau's head; and Esau's head rolled until it entered the cave and came to rest in the bosom of his father Isaac.

paragraphs.text: Bereishit Rabbah 51:11: "Rabbi Yudan in the name of Rabbi Aibu: Because the elder daughter disgraced her father's honor and declared his name 'Moab,' meaning 'from father' (me-av)... (it was permitted to intimidate and harass them); whereas regarding the younger daughter, because she spared her father's honor and said: 'And she called his name Ben-Ammi' (Genesis 19:38), meaning 'the son of the one who was with me'... Scripture states: 'Do not distress them and do not provoke them' (Deuteronomy 2:19) at all."

paragraphs.text: Megillah 6a: "Caesarea and Jerusalem: If someone tells you, 'Both are destroyed,' do not believe him; 'Both are inhabited,' do not believe him. 'Caesarea is destroyed and Jerusalem is inhabited,' or 'Jerusalem is destroyed and Caesarea is inhabited,' believe him. As it is stated: 'I shall be filled, now that she is laid waste' (Ezekiel 26:2): if this one is full, that one is laid waste; if that one is full, this one is laid waste. Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: It is derived from here: 'And one nation shall grow stronger than the other nation' (Genesis 25:23)."

paragraphs.text: Bava Batra 74b: "Rav Yehudah said in the name of Rav: Everything that the Holy One, blessed be He, created in His world, He created male and female. Even Leviathan the slant serpent and Leviathan the tortuous serpent He created male and female; and were they to mate with one another, they would destroy the entire world. What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He castrated the male, and slew the female and salted her away for the righteous in the Time to Come, as it is stated: 'And He will slay the sea monster that is in the sea' (Isaiah 27:1). And likewise Behemot upon a thousand hills He created male and female; and were they to mate with one another, they would destroy the entire world. What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He castrated the male, cooled the female, and preserved her for the righteous in the Time to Come, as it is stated: 'Behold now Behemot, which I made with you... Behold now, his strength is in his loins, etc.' (Job 40:15–16)." Our Master explained this matter in Likutei Maamarim, p. 100, and in Dover Tzedek, p. 159.

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 10a: The Talmud relates that King Chizkiyahu refrained from marrying and having children because he foresaw through Divine Inspiration (ruach hakodesh) that wicked sons were destined to issue from him. The prophet Yeshayahu told him that he would be punished for this, since his obligation was to fulfill the mitzvah to be fruitful and multiply, whereas what would become of his children belongs to "the hidden mysteries of the Merciful One" (kivshei d'Rachamana) — Divine calculations that were not his affair. Ultimately Chizkiyahu married, and indeed a wicked son was born to him, namely King Menasheh. According to our Author (Rav Tzadok), at times the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself withholds the blessing of physical children from righteous individuals because He knows that good would not come of it, and this is part of His blessed calculations.

paragraphs.text: Shemot Rabbah 32:1: "'And the writing was the writing of God, engraved (charut) upon the Tablets' (Shemot 32:16). What is the meaning of charut? Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Nechemyah expounded it: Rabbi Yehudah says it means freedom (cheirut) from exiles (foreign kingdoms), and Rabbi Nechemyah says it means freedom (cheirut) from the Angel of Death."

paragraphs.text: Rambam, Hilkhot Melakhim 5:5: "Likewise, it is a positive commandment to destroy the remembrance of Amalek, as it is stated: 'You shall blot out the remembrance of Amalek' (Devarim 25:19); and it is a positive commandment to remember continually his evil deeds and his ambush, so as to keep enmity toward him awakened, as it is stated: 'Remember what Amalek did to you' (Devarim 25:17). From the Oral Tradition the Sages taught: 'Remember' — verbally with the mouth; 'Do not forget' — inwardly in the heart, for it is forbidden to forget enmity and hatred toward him."

paragraphs.text: Yoma 69b: "And they cried out with a loud voice to Hashem, God" (Nechemyah 9:4). Rav — and some say Rabbi Yochanan — said: They cried out because the evil inclination for idolatry had caused the destruction of the Sanctuary, the burning of the Temple Hall, the slaying of all the righteous, and the exile of Israel from their Land, and yet it was still dancing among them to cause them to sin! "Did You not give it to us only so that we might receive reward for overcoming it? We want neither it nor its reward!" ... They fasted for three days and three nights, and Heaven delivered it over to them. It came forth like a fiery lion cub from the Chamber of the Holy of Holies, and the prophet (Zekharyah) told them: "This is the inclination for idolatry." They cast it into a lead cauldron and sealed its mouth with lead so that its voice would not be heard. They then prayed also concerning the inclination for sexual immorality, and it too was delivered into their hands. The prophet warned them that if they killed it, the world would perish; they imprisoned it for three days and searched throughout all the Land of Israel for a fresh egg for a sick person and could not find one (since the urge for procreation had been nullified)... So they blinded its eyes and released it, which accomplished that a person's passion is no longer aroused toward his own close blood relatives.

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 89b: "Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of Rabbi Yonatan: What is the meaning of that which is written, 'For You are our Father, though Avraham does not know us and Yisrael does not recognize us; You, Hashem, are our Father, our Redeemer from everlasting is Your Name' (Yeshayahu 63:16)? In the Future to Come, the Holy One, blessed be He, will say to Avraham: 'Your children have sinned against Me.' He will reply before Him: 'Master of the Universe, let them be wiped out for the sanctification of Your Name!' Hashem will say to Himself: 'Let Me say this to Yaakov, who experienced the pain of raising children; perhaps he will beg for mercy upon them.' So He will say to him: 'Your children have sinned.' Yaakov too will reply before Him: 'Master of the Universe, let them be wiped out for the sanctification of Your Name!' Hashem will say: 'There is neither reason among the elders, nor counsel among the young.' He will then say to Yitzchak: 'Your children have sinned against Me.' Yitzchak will reply before Him: 'Master of the Universe, are they my children and not Your children?! At Sinai, when they gave precedence before You to "We will do" over "We will hear," You called them "My son, My firstborn" — and now they are my children and not Your children?! Furthermore, how much could they possibly have sinned? How many are the years of a person's life? Seventy years. Subtract twenty years, for which You do not punish — fifty remain. Subtract twenty-five years of nights — twenty-five remain. Subtract twelve and a half years spent praying, eating, and attending to bodily needs — twelve and a half years remain! If You will bear all of them Yourself, well and good; and if not, let half be upon me and half upon You. And should You say that all of them must be upon me — behold, I already offered myself up before You upon the altar!' Immediately Israel will open their mouths and exclaim to Yitzchak: '(For) you are our father!' Yitzchak will say to them: 'Instead of praising me, praise the Holy One, blessed be He!' And Yitzchak will show them the Holy One, blessed be He, before their very eyes. Immediately they will lift their eyes on high and declare: 'You, Hashem, are our Father; our Redeemer from everlasting is Your Name!'"

paragraphs.text: Avodah Zarah 65a: "He went and found him sitting up to his neck in rosewater (Rava went and found Bar Sheshakh sitting in a bath of roses) while naked harlots stood before him. Bar Sheshakh said to him: 'Do you have anything like this in the World to Come?' Rava replied: 'Ours is far superior to this!' He asked him: 'Could there possibly be anything greater than this?' Rava said to him: 'Upon you lies the dread of the ruling power, whereas upon us there will be no dread of any ruling power.' Bar Sheshakh replied: 'As for me, at least, what dread of the ruling power lies upon me?' While they were still sitting together, a royal courier arrived and said to him: 'Arise, for the king summons you!' As he was departing, Bar Sheshakh said to Rava: 'May the eye that wishes to see evil befall you burst!' Rava answered: 'Amen.' And Bar Sheshakh's eye burst."

paragraphs.text: Sifrei DeAggadeta Esther 1: "Rabbi Yudan and Rabbi Levi said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: Wherever 'King Achashverosh' is stated in Megillat Esther, Scripture speaks of Achashverosh; and wherever 'the King' is stated without qualification, Scripture speaks (also) of the King of kings of kings — thus 'when the heart of the King was merry with wine' means when the heart of the Holy One, blessed be He, was merry with the wine of Torah."

paragraphs.text: Avodah Zarah 8a: "It was taught in a Baraita: Rabbi Yishmael says: Israelites who dwell outside the Land of Israel worship idolatry in purity. How so? If an idolater makes a banquet for his son and invites all the Jews in his town, even though they eat of their own food and drink of their own wine and their own attendant stands waiting upon them, Scripture accounts it to them as though they had eaten from sacrifices offered to the dead (idols), as it is stated: 'And he will invite you, and you will eat of his sacrifice' (Shemot 34:15). One might ask: Say this applies only once he actually eats of it! Rava replied: If so, let Scripture state merely 'and you will eat of his sacrifice'; why state 'And he will invite you'? To teach that culpability begins from the very moment of accepting the invitation."

paragraphs.text: Megillah 16a Tosafot: "I heard that Haman's ten thousand talents (kikkar) of silver equaled one half-shekel per person for each of the Israelites, who numbered six hundred thousand when they went forth from Egypt; thus Haman declared that he would pay Achashverosh their entire ransom-value — examine the calculation closely and you will find it exact."

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah 4a: Rabbi Yitzchak states in the Gemara that Darius (Artaxerxes) became wicked despite having contributed sacrifices, because he stipulated that he was doing so in order that the priests pray for his life and the life of his sons; and the Gemara challenges this: "Was it not taught in a Baraita: One who says, 'This sela is for charity so that my son may live, or so that I may merit through it the life of the World to Come' — behold, such a person is completely righteous?! There is no contradiction: here it speaks of Israelites; there it speaks of gentiles."

paragraphs.text: Megillah 12b: "'And those closest (ve-hakarov) to him were Karshena, Shetar, Admata, Tarshish, [Meres, Marsena, Memukhan]' (Esther 1:14). Rabbi Levi said: This entire verse was stated with reference to the sacrifices (korbanot): Karshena — the ministering angels pleaded before the Holy One, blessed be He: 'Master of the Universe, have the nations ever offered before You yearling lambs (karim bnei shanah) the way Israel offered before You?' Shetar — 'Have they ever offered before You two turtledoves (shtei torin)?' Admata — 'Have they ever built before You an altar of earth (mizbach adamah)?' Tarshish — 'Have they ever ministered before You in priestly vestments, concerning which is written tarshish (chrysolite), onyx, and jasper?' Meres — 'Have they ever stirred (mirsu) the sacrificial blood before You?' Marsena — 'Have they ever stirred (mirsu) the meal-offerings before You?' Memukhan — 'Have they ever prepared (hekhinu) the Showbread Table before You?'"

Kabbalah: Sha'ar HaPesukim, Parashat Chayei Sarah 8-15 — “… ההוא רוחא דשדי בה בגווה שבמלכות אשר על ידו עולים המן מהנוקבא לגבי דכורא כנודע וזס כלב והשלים מה שהתחיל אליעזר לתקן …”. paragraphs.text: Megillah 15a & Rashi: Megillah 15a: "Rabbi Abba said: It will not be according to the custom — for on every single day until now it was under compulsion, whereas now it is willingly. 'And if I perish, I perish' — just as I became lost from my father's house, so too shall I become lost from you." Rashi ibid.: "'I shall become lost from you' — meaning, I will become forbidden to you, for a married Israelite woman who was violated under compulsion remains permitted to her husband, whereas if she acted willingly, she becomes forbidden to her husband."

paragraphs.text: Shocher Tov 22:24: Shocher Tov 22:24: "'Be not far from Me, for trouble is near.' When was this said? At the time when Achashverosh decreed to destroy, to slay, and to annihilate. At that hour Esther entered without permission, as it is stated: 'And she stood in the inner court of the king's house.' The king had seven partitioned chambers; she entered the first chamber, the second, and the third... Once she reached the seventh chamber, Achashverosh's wrath burned and he gnashed his teeth. He said: 'Woe to such disgrace! I desired and requested Queen Vashti to enter before me, and she refused to enter, as it is stated: "But Queen Vashti refused," so I decreed execution upon her — and now this one enters like a harlot without permission!'... At that moment an angel descended from Heaven, struck him across his mouth, and said to him: 'Wicked one! Your royal lady stands outside, while you sit inside?' It is not written vayehi bi-re'ot ha-melekh ('and it came to pass when the king looked'), but rather vayehi khi-re'ot ('and it came to pass as the king saw') — against his will and against his inclination, she found favor in his eyes."

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 65a, Rashi & Tosafot: Sanhedrin 65a: "Regarding a blasphemer, what action is there? The moving of his lips constitutes an action." Rashi: "'Since it depends on the heart' — the primary liability incurred by him depends on the heart, namely that he intends to curse (euphemistically, 'bless') the Divine Name; for even if he curses (lit., 'blesses') the Name all day long, yet in his heart it is not directed toward On High — rather, he assigned the Name to some other object, calling it by the Ineffable Name and cursing that object — he is not liable." And in Tosafot ibid.: "Since it is written regarding Nineveh: 'From you went forth one who devises evil against Hashem' — referring to Ravshakeh, who blasphemed and was the emissary of Sancheriv king of Assyria, Nineveh being in the land of Assyria — Scripture thus made blasphemy contingent upon thought."

paragraphs.text: Tanchuma Noach 3: "And this is the Oral Torah, which is difficult to learn and involves great distress, for it is compared to darkness, as it is said: 'The people who walk in darkness have seen a great light' (Yeshayahu 9:1) — these are the masters of the Talmud, who have seen a great light, for the Holy One, blessed be He, illuminates their eyes regarding what is forbidden and permitted, impure and pure. And in the Future to Come: 'And those who love Him shall be like the sun going forth in its might' (Shoftim 5:31)." And further on there: "And in the second passage (of Shema) it is written: 'with all your heart and with all your soul' (Devarim 11:13), and it is not written 'with all your might (wealth),' to teach you that anyone who loves wealth and pleasure cannot learn the Oral Torah, because it involves great distress and sleeplessness, and one wears himself out and makes himself unsightly over it; therefore, the bestowal of its reward is in the World to Come, as it is said: 'The people who walk in darkness have seen a great light.'"

paragraphs.text: Kiddushin 29b: "Abaye heard that he was coming (he heard that Rav Acha had arrived at his locale). There was a certain demon in Abaye's study hall, such that even when people entered in pairs during the daytime, they would be harmed. He said to them: 'Let no man offer him lodging; perhaps a miracle will occur.' He entered and spent the night in that study hall. It appeared to him like a seven-headed serpent. With every bow that he bowed (in prayer), one of its heads fell off. The next day he said to them: 'Had a miracle not occurred, you would have endangered me!'" And in Rashi: "'Let no man offer him lodging' — to Rav Acha, so that against his will he would lodge in the study hall, and through his piety a miracle would be wrought for him and he would slay the demon."

paragraphs.text: Sukkah 20b, in the Mishnah: "And Rabban Gamliel said to the Elders: 'Have you seen Tavi my servant, who is a Torah scholar and knows that servants are exempt from the sukkah, and therefore he sleeps beneath the bed?' And incidentally, according to our way, we learned that one who sleeps beneath the bed has not fulfilled his obligation." And in the Gemara, 21b: "It was taught in a Baraita: Rabbi Shimon said: From the casual conversation of Rabban Gamliel we learned two things: we learned that servants are exempt from the sukkah, and we learned that one who sleeps beneath the bed has not fulfilled his obligation. Yet let him say: 'From the words of Rabban Gamliel'! He teaches us something in passing, in accordance with that which Rav Acha bar Adda said — and some say Rav Acha bar Adda said that Rav Hamnuna said that Rav said: From where do we know that even the casual conversation of Torah scholars requires study? Because it is said: 'And whose leaf does not wither' (Tehillim 1:3)."

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 99b: "Rabbi Elazar said: Every person was created for toil, as it is said: 'For man is born for toil' (Iyov 5:7). I do not know whether he was created for toil of the mouth or whether he was created for toil of labor; when Scripture says: 'For his mouth urges him on' (Mishlei 16:26), you must say he was created for toil of the mouth. Yet I still do not know whether for toil of Torah or for toil of conversation; when Scripture says: 'This Book of the Torah shall not depart from your mouth' (Yehoshua 1:8), you must say he was created for toil of Torah."

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 8a: "Abaye said: Initially I used to study inside the house and pray in the synagogue. Once I heard that which Rabbi Chiya bar Ami said in the name of Ulla: 'From the day the Holy Temple was destroyed, the Holy One, blessed be He, has nothing in His world except the four cubits of halakhah alone' — I would pray only in the place where I studied." And in Megillah 29a: "Abaye said: Initially I used to study in the house and pray in the synagogue. Once I heard that which David said: 'Hashem, I love the abode of Your house' (Tehillim 26:8), I came to study in the synagogue."

paragraphs.text: Bava Metzia 59b: "He (Rabbi Eliezer) said to them (the Sages): 'If the halakhah accords with me, let Heaven prove it!' A Heavenly Voice (Bat Kol) went forth and declared: 'What have you against Rabbi Eliezer, for the halakhah accords with him in every place!' Rabbi Yehoshua stood on his feet and declared: 'It is not in Heaven!' (Devarim 30:12). What does 'It is not in Heaven' mean? Rabbi Yirmeyahu said: 'Since the Torah was already given from Mount Sinai, we pay no heed to a Heavenly Voice, for You already wrote at Mount Sinai in the Torah: Follow the majority (Shemot 23:2).' Rabbi Natan encountered Eliyahu and said to him: 'What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do at that hour?' He replied to him: 'He smiled and said: My children have defeated Me, My children have defeated Me!'" And in Pesachim 119a: "Rav Kahana said in the name of Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yose: What is the meaning of that which is written: 'For the Conductor (lamenatze'ach), a Psalm of David'? Sing praises to the One who rejoices when they defeat Him."

paragraphs.text: Tanchuma Ki Tisa 34: "Rabbi Yehudah bar Shalom said: When the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moshe, 'Write for yourself' (Shemot 34:27), Moshe requested that the Mishnah also be in writing. However, because the Holy One, blessed be He, foresaw that the nations of the world were destined to translate the Torah and read it in Greek and declare, 'We are Israel'... the Holy One, blessed be He, said to the idolaters: 'You claim that you are My children? I recognize only that those who possess My secret mystery (mistorin) are My children!' And what is it? That is the Mishnah, which was given orally."

paragraphs.text: Parallels. Halachah: Shulchan Aruch HaRav, Orach Chayim 3:9-10 — “… שאי אפשר לו בקלות להסב מטתו בין צפון לדרום — אין עליו אסור לשמש מטתו בין מזרח למערב. ויש לסמך על ספר …”. Talmud Bavli: Eruvin 38a — “… אליעזר אומר: יום טוב הסמוך לשבת, בין מלפניה ובין מלאחריה — מערב אדם שני עירובין, ואומר: עירובי בראשון למזרח ובשני למערב; בראשון …”. Meforshei HaShas: Rashi on Berakhot 5b:22:1 — “צפון לדרום – ראשה ומרגלותיה זה לצפון וזה לדרום. ונראה בעיני שהשכינה במזרח או במערב לפיכך נכון להסב דרך תשמיש לרוחות אחרות:”. Talmud Yerushalmi: Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 3:7 — “משנה: רבי אליעזר אומר יום טוב שהוא סמוך לשבת בין מלפניה בין מלאחריה מערב אדם שני עירובין ואומר עירובי הראשון למזרח והשני …”. Meforshei HaYerushalmi: Penei Moshe on Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 3:7 — “… השני יקנה לי ליום השני לילך למערב או איפכא הראשון למערב והשני למזרח כפי שהוא צריך משום דקסבר רבי אליעזר יום טוב …”. Mishnah: Mishnah Eruvin 3:6 — “רבי אליעזר אומר, יום טוב הסמוך לשבת, בין מלפניה ובין מלאחריה, מערב אדם שני ערובין ואומר, ערובי הראשון למזרח, והשני למערב. הראשון …”. Meforshei HaMishnah: Bartenura on Mishnah Eruvin 3:6 — “… צריך לילך יום ראשון לכאן ויום שני לכאן, יכול לערב למזרח ולמערב ערב יום הראשון, ואומר ערובי של מזרח יקנה לי היום …”. paragraphs.text: Megillah 10b: "Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi opened his exposition of this portion from here: 'And it shall come to pass, that just as Hashem rejoiced over you to do you good... so will Hashem cause others to rejoice to destroy you' (Devarim 28:63). Now does the Holy One, blessed be He, rejoice in the downfall of the wicked? Surely it is written: 'as they went out before the vanguard, and said: Give thanks to Hashem, for His kindness endures forever' (Divrei HaYamim II 20:21), concerning which Rabbi Yochanan said: Why was 'for He is good' omitted from this thanksgiving? Because the Holy One, blessed be He, does not rejoice in the downfall of the wicked! And Rabbi Yochanan further said: What is the meaning of that which is written: 'And one did not come near the other all the night' (Shemot 14:20)? The ministering angels sought to recite song, and the Holy One, blessed be He, said: The work of My hands is drowning in the sea, and you wish to recite song?! Rabbi Elazar said: He Himself does not rejoice, yet He causes others to rejoice. A precise reading of the verse supports this as well, for it is written 'so will He cause to rejoice' (yasis), and it is not written 'He will rejoice' (yasus). Learn from this that it is so."

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Bereishit 36b (Sulam translation): "At first they had 'garments of light' (kotnot or), which the celestial beings used on high, for supernal angels would come to Adam HaRishon to derive benefit from that light, as it is stated: 'Yet You have made him slightly less than the angels, and have crowned him with glory and majesty' (Tehillim 8:6). Now that they sinned, however, they were given 'garments of skin' (kotnot or), from which only the skin derives benefit — namely, the body and not the soul."

paragraphs.text: Kiddushin 70a: "A Tanna taught... Whoever disqualifies others is himself blemished... And Shmuel said: With his own blemish he disqualifies others. There was a certain man from Nehardea who went into a butcher shop in Pumbedita and said to them: 'Give me meat!' They said to him: 'Wait until the attendant of Rav Yehudah bar Yechezkel takes his portion, and then we will give some to you.' He said: 'Who is this Yehudah bar Sheviskel (a mocking distortion meaning "glutton") who precedes me to take before me?' They went and told Rav Yehudah, who placed him under a ban of excommunication. They then told Rav Yehudah: 'He is accustomed to calling people slaves.' Whereupon Rav Yehudah publicly proclaimed concerning him that he himself was a slave (one who habitually calls other people slaves — proclaim concerning him that he is a slave)."

paragraphs.text: Bava Kamma 117a: "There was a certain man who wanted to inform on his fellow's straw (meaning, he wanted to denounce his fellow's straw to the authorities). He came before Rav, who said to him: 'Do not inform, and do not inform!' He replied to him: 'I will inform, and I will inform!' Rav Kahana was sitting before Rav, and he snapped the man's neck from him (killing him). Rav applied to him the verse: 'Your sons have fainted; they lie at the head of all the streets like an antelope in a net' (Yeshayahu 51:20) — just as with this antelope, once it falls into a net, they have no mercy upon it, so too with the property of a Jew, once it falls into the hands of idolaters, they have no mercy upon it."

paragraphs.text: Bava Batra 123b: "Rabbi Chelbo inquired of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani: It is written, 'And it came to pass, when Rachel had borne Yosef, etc.' (Bereishit 30:25). Why specifically when Yosef was born (did Yaakov ask to depart)? He replied to him: Our Patriarch Yaakov foresaw that the descendants of Esav would be delivered only into the hands of the descendants of Yosef, as it is stated: 'And the house of Yaakov shall be a fire, and the house of Yosef a flame, and the house of Esav for stubble' (Ovadiah 1:18)."
