paragraphs.text: Bava Batra 12a–b: "Ameimar said: And a sage is greater than a prophet, as it is stated: 'That we may bring (navi, homiletically read as 'a prophet') a heart of wisdom' (Tehillim 90:12). Who is dependent upon whom? You must say: The lesser is dependent upon the greater... Rather, Rav Ashi said: Know that this is so, for a great man states a matter of Torah through his own reasoning, and afterward a Halachah leMoshe miSinai (an oral law transmitted to Moshe at Sinai) is stated in accordance with his words." (The proof that Torah wisdom possesses an aspect of prophecy is that a great sage formulates a Torah insight, and it becomes clear that this very ruling is a Halachah leMoshe miSinai.)

paragraphs.text: Mekhilta DeRabbi Yishmael, Beshalach (Massekhta DeShirah 4) & Mekhilta DeRashbi 20:5: Mekhilta DeRabbi Yishmael, Beshalach — Massekhta DeShirah 4: "'Hashem is a Man of War' (Exodus 15:3) — why is this stated? Because He revealed Himself at the Sea as a mighty warrior waging war, as it is said, 'Hashem is a Man of War'; whereas He revealed Himself at Sinai as an elder full of compassion, as it is said, 'And they saw the God of Israel' (Exodus 24:10)." Mekhilta DeRashbi 20:5: "'I am Hashem your God' (Exodus 20:2) — this teaches that they beheld the Countenance destined to pay reward to the righteous in the Time to Come. And in view of the fact that the prophets convey visions of Him in varied expressions — one verse says, 'His garment was white as snow' (Daniel 7:9), while another verse says, 'Why is Your apparel red?' (Isaiah 63:2)."

paragraphs.text: Bamidbar 28:26–30 & Yerushalmi Rosh Hashanah 4:8: Bamidbar 28:26–30: "And on the Day of the Firstfruits, when you bring a new meal-offering to Hashem on your Festival of Weeks, you shall have a sacred convocation; you shall do no laborious work... one male goat to make atonement for you" — whereas regarding the he-goats of the other festivals, it is explicitly mentioned that they are "for a sin-offering" (lechatat). Yerushalmi Rosh Hashanah 4:8: "Rabbi Mesharshiya in the name of Rabbi Idi: Regarding all the other festival offerings 'sin' (chet) is written, whereas regarding Atzeret (Shavuot) 'sin' is not written. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to them: 'Since you accepted upon yourselves the yoke of Torah, I ascribe it to you as though you had never sinned in all your days.'"

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 35b: "Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa said: Whoever derives benefit from this world without a blessing is as though he robs the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Congregation of Israel, as it is stated: 'He who robs his father and his mother and says, "It is no transgression," is a companion to a destroyer' (Proverbs 28:24). And 'his father' refers solely to the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is stated: 'Is He not your Father, who acquired you?' (Deuteronomy 32:6); and 'his mother' refers solely to the Congregation of Israel, as it is stated: 'Hear, my son, the instruction of your father, and do not forsake the Torah of your mother' (Proverbs 1:8)."

paragraphs.text: Zohar Part I, Midrash HaNe'elam 128b (translated): "Come and see: Initially, when the evil inclination was cast into this world, it was called Lot ('cursed' or 'shrouded'). In the World to Come, it will be nullified from the world, yet not entirely; rather, it will be called Lavan ('white') — no longer repulsive as at first, but like one who has bathed from his filth. For what purpose will Lavan be needed? Rabbi Shimon said: It will be needed to engage in procreation ('be fruitful and multiply'), for Rabbi Shimon said: If the evil inclination is not present, procreation is not found."

paragraphs.text: Shemot Rabbah 41:3: "This may be compared to a wealthy man who had a son. When the son returned from school, his father gave him a portion of food. His son said to him: 'I desire only some of the sweet delicacy (potztelin) that is inside your mouth.' So he took it and gave it to him from within his mouth. Thus it is written: Not merely 'For Hashem gives wisdom,' rather, 'from His mouth come knowledge and understanding' (Proverbs 2:6)."

paragraphs.text: Menachot 29b: "Rav Yehudah said in the name of Rav: When Moshe ascended on high, he found the Holy One, blessed be He, sitting and tying crowns onto the letters of the Torah. He said before Him: 'Master of the Universe, who stays Your hand?' He said to him: 'There is one man who is destined to arise at the end of several generations, and Akiva ben Yosef is his name, who is destined to expound upon every single tittle heaps upon heaps of laws.' He said before Him: 'Master of the Universe, show him to me.' He said to him: 'Turn behind you.' Moshe went and sat at the back of eight rows of disciples, and he did not understand what they were saying; his strength flagged. Once Rabbi Akiva reached a certain topic, his disciples said to him: 'Rabbi, from where do you know this?' He said to them: 'It is a law transmitted to Moshe from Sinai.' Thereupon Moshe's mind was set at ease. He returned and came before the Holy One, blessed be He, and said before Him: 'Master of the Universe, You have a man such as this, and yet You give the Torah through me?' He said to him: 'Be silent; so it arose in thought before Me.' He said before Him: 'Master of the Universe, You have shown me his Torah; show me his reward.' He said to him: 'Turn behind you.' He turned behind him and saw them weighing Rabbi Akiva's flesh in the butcher stalls. He said before Him: 'Master of the Universe, such is Torah, and such is its reward?' He said to him: 'Be silent; so it arose in thought before Me.'"

Talmud Bavli: Sanhedrin 84a — “תרי תנאי ואליבא דרבי עקיבא. מתניתין – רבי שמעון ואליבא דרבי עקיבא. ברייתא – רבנן ואליבא דרבי עקיבא. הדרן עלך אלו הן …”. Talmud Yerushalmi: Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 1:4 — “… כיין הטוב. שמעון בר ווא בשם רבי יוחנן דודים דברי סופרים לדברי תורה וחביבין יותר מדברי תורה. כי טובים דודיך מיין. רבי …”. Meforshei HaYerushalmi: Korban HaEdah on Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 11:4 — “מתני' חומר מדברי סופרים. דברים שנפרשו על פי הקבלה איש מפי איש או בי"ג מדות שהתורה נדרשת בהן מדברים המפורשים בתורה: האומר …”. Mishnah: Mishnah Sanhedrin 11:3 — “חמר בדברי סופרים מבדברי תורה, האומר אין תפלין, כדי לעבר על דברי תורה, פטור. חמשה טוטפות, להוסיף על דברי סופרים, חיב:”. Meforshei HaMidrash: Etz Yosef on Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:2:7:3-4 — “… לתורה, שהפירושים במדרגת הפנים והצורות (יפה עינים): שנאמר כי טובים דודיך מיין. והכי קאמר קרא ישקני מנשיקות פיהו הוא תורה שבעל פה, …”. paragraphs.text: Tanchuma Ki Tisa 31: "Because the First Tablets were given in public, the evil eye had power over them and they were broken; whereas here (regarding the Second Tablets), the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: 'Nothing is more becoming than modesty,' as it is stated: 'And what does Hashem require of you, if not to do justice, to love kindness, and to walk modestly with your God?' (Micah 6:8)."
